title: Complete Shutter Down Paralyzes Rawalakot Poonch as Thousands Protest Against Punitive Measures, Power Cuts and Communication Blackouts
excerpt: Thousands shut down Rawalakot in protest against prolonged electricity outages, low voltage supply, and communication blackouts across District Poonch.
author: Special Correspondent, Rawalakot AK

heroImage.caption: Residents protest prolonged power cuts and communication blackouts in Rawalakot.

body.text: A complete shutter down brought life to a standstill in Rawalakot on Monday as thousands of residents from across District Poonch poured into the streets to protest prolonged power outages, severe load shedding, low voltage electricity, and persistent internet and mobile network disruptions.

Markets remained closed and traffic was largely halted as protesters marched through the city and gathered near the grid station, demanding an immediate end to what they described as collective punishment of the population.

items: Access to essential services is a state obligation
Emergency powers must not violate freedoms

body.caption: Protesters gather near the grid station demanding restoration of electricity.

body.text: Residents say Azad Kashmir has faced extreme load shedding for several months, with the Poonch region experiencing between 15 and 20 hours of power cuts daily.
Small businesses dependent on electricity and digital connectivity are struggling. Hospitals, clinics, schools, and universities report serious disruptions.

body.caption: Shuttered markets during the complete shutdown in Rawalakot.

body.text: Millions of Kashmiris living abroad report difficulty contacting their families due to prolonged power outages and failing communication networks.
Public frustration has been building for more than two and a half years. Previous protests forced authorities to promise electricity at production cost and improvements in essential infrastructure.
Protesters accuse authorities of responding to legitimate democratic demands with force, intimidation, and disinformation.
Azad Kashmir produces more than 4,000 megawatts of electricity, while its daily requirement is estimated at only 350 to 400 megawatts.
Rights activists cite findings from UN and European Parliament reports documenting serious human rights concerns.
Protesters announced an indefinite sit-in in Rawalakot, calling for restoration of reliable electricity and communication services.
